title: Proteomic Data Processing and Matrisome Annotation of Human Placenta LC-MS/MS Data
author: Amanpreet K. Bains
materials: Import of Raw Mass Spectrometry Data
Import raw LC-MS/MS files into MaxQuant (version 2.0.3.1).
Specify the digestion enzyme as strict trypsin.
Allow a maximum of two missed cleavage sites.
Use normalized TPI values for downstream comparative analyses.

steps.title: Configure MaxQuant Database Search
steps.instruction: Configure the database search using the uniprotkb_Human_reviewed_2025_03_10 human protein database with the following parameters:

substeps.instruction: Enable MaxQuant LFQ for label-free quantification using default software settings
Set parent ion mass tolerance to 10 ppm
Set fragment ion mass tolerance to 20 ppm
Set carbamidomethylation of cysteine residues as a fixed modification

Set the following variable modifications: N-terminal glutamine to pyroglutamate conversion (Gln→pyro-Glu), deamidation of asparagine, deamidation of glutamine, oxidation of methionine, oxidation of proline, and oxidation of lysine

steps.title: Validate Identifications in Scaffold
steps.instruction: Import MaxQuant search results into Scaffold (version 5.2.2, Proteome Software Inc., Portland, OR) and apply the following validation criteria:

substeps.instruction: Accept peptide identifications only if they achieve a false discovery rate (FDR) below 1.0% by the Percolator posterior error probability calculation
Accept protein identifications only if the protein FDR is below 1.0% and at least two unique peptides are identified per protein
Assign protein probabilities using the Protein Prophet algorithm
Group proteins sharing similar peptides according to the principles of parsimony when proteins cannot be distinguished solely by MS/MS evidence

steps.title: Annotate Proteins via Matrisome AnalyzeR
steps.instruction: Import validated protein identification data into Matrisome AnalyzeR to annotate proteins as ECM or non-ECM components using the following classification hierarchy:

substeps.instruction: Classify matrisome proteins into Core matrisome components or Matrisome-associated components
Further classify core matrisome proteins into ECM glycoproteins, Collagens, or Proteoglycans
Further classify matrisome-associated proteins into ECM-affiliated proteins, ECM regulators, or Secreted factors

steps.title: Quantify and Normalize Protein Abundance
steps.instruction: Use total precursor ion intensity (TPI) values for label-free inter-group quantification and estimation of protein abundance:

substeps.instruction: Calculate a scaling factor for each sample: Scaling factor = (Total TPI of sample) / (Minimum total TPI across all samples)
Normalize protein TPI values within each sample using the corresponding sample-specific scaling factor to bring all samples to a common intensity level
